newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Texaco unit joins Venezuelan lubricants mkt.
newsitem.headline: Texaco unit joins Venezuelan lubricants mkt.

text.p: U.S. oil company Texaco Inc will invest $10 million in Venezuela's lubricants market over the medium term through its Texaco Services Inc unit, a company official said Monday.

"Venezuela is one of the markets with greatest growth potential in Latin America and also has the largest oil and natural gas reserves in the western hemisphere," Marcos Avalos, general manager of Texaco Services Venezuela, told a news conference.

Texaco has reached agreement with local investors to use a processing plant in Cagua, central Venezuela, with a capacity equivalent to 8,000 metric tonnes per year. Other plans will be incorporated in the future, Avalos said.
Venezuela's lubricants market, including kerosene, asphalts and solvents, totaled 43,000 barrels per day in 1995, according to state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela.
Avalos said Texaco hoped to export approximately 15 percent of its Venezuelan-produced lubricants to neighboring countries in the future.
